fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jack Kelley returns to InnerVerse to discuss his new book, the Atlantis Puzzle. Going beyond the search for a geographical location, Jack's new book uncovers powerful esoteric themes in Plato's writings. This conversation explores the absence of esotericism from academic discourse, the eternal schism between philosophical theory and rational praxis, the ways in which the Atlantis allegory provides important insights into the degradation of modern society, and why mythic literacy may be essential for civilization's psychological stability.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Mistranslation That Moved Atlantis", "body": "George Sarantitis spent two years retranslating Plato and found that the water you cross to reach Atlantis is not the Atlantic Ocean but the Atlantic Pelagos, a word the Greeks reserved for an inland sea rather than Okeanos. Earlier translators, who had never heard of such a sea, reached for the ocean they did know. Read with an awareness of long term climate change, the corrected geography points not to a sunken continent but to a landmass laced with waterways in North Africa, where the Green Sahara once held mega lakes the size of modern Germany."}, {"title": "A Real Setting Is Not a True Story", "body": "Jack's Hamlet analogy carries this one. Shakespeare set his play at Elsinore, a real castle called Kronborg, because the queen of England was Danish and had married there, yet the original Amleth was a pre-Viking prince from Jutland with no connection to the place. A real map does not make a real story. The rush to crown the Richat Structure as the Atlantean capital misses what Sarantitis never claimed, and Herodotus scattering the Amazons across Africa, the Caucasus, India and Thrace shows how freely ancient authors cobbled bits and pieces together."}, {"title": "The Pillars Were Never in One Place", "body": "What we translate as pillar is stelae, commemorative markers the Greeks left at the furthest extent of a voyage, so as seafaring expanded the pillars drifted further afield. Tacitus put them in northern Germany, other authors inside or outside Gibraltar, and they were variously called rocks, islands or temple columns. Plato, Jack argues, could not resist relocating them to show that nobody in his era knew what they were talking about. Diodorus even identified Heracles with the sun, which opens the pillars onto the equinoctial gates of the year."}, {"title": "Plato Writing Through Homer", "body": "Leaving Critias as a cliffhanger points the reader back to the opening of the Odyssey, where Poseidon is missing from the council of gods because he is in Africa feasting with the Ethiopians, a blessed people said to dwell split in two, some where the sun rises and some where he sets. That scene then redirects again to the council of gods in the Iliad, a double layer of redirection hinting at cycles and distant eras. Chance finds the same habit in the sky, where constellations were read as text and punning between languages counted as divine revelation."}, {"title": "Deep Time and the Myth of Progress", "body": "The physical side of the story turns out to be as strange as the myth. Obsidian runs of eighty kilometers by boat, stone tools on Crete reaching back 130,000 years on an island detached for five million, Neanderthal tools on islands never joined to the mainland, butchered rhino bones in Indonesia close to a million years old. Science keeps revising the dates while leaving the story of primitive ancestors intact. Chance notes that carbon dating calibrates itself in a circle, and Jack closes by tracing Plato's conflict from empires down into a single divided mind."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "What a good esoteric writer really does in the first place, like Plato, is it's up to you to puzzle out which is which.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Some of our ancestors were dumber than us, and some were smarter. It's not all or nothing. It's somewhere in the middle.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Ancient authors were often confused about things just as modernity has been.", "author": "Jack Kelley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d548e142-2d5c-455e-8a3c-bc08780bea32/JACK-KELLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There was more than one Hercules in the ancient mythology of the Mediterranean world.", "author": "Jack Kelley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d548e142-2d5c-455e-8a3c-bc08780bea32/JACK-KELLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The sun is the thing that is a unifying story for all peoples.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "It is part of the mystery school tradition to receive gnosis from the heavens via wordplay and punning in the stars.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There was no PlayStation or Xbox or movie theaters. So what did people do at night? They told stories, and they looked up at the stars.", "author": "Jack Kelley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d548e142-2d5c-455e-8a3c-bc08780bea32/JACK-KELLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "People have been sailing the Mediterranean, without a doubt, for at least 130,000 years.", "author": "Jack Kelley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d548e142-2d5c-455e-8a3c-bc08780bea32/JACK-KELLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The higher perspective you reach, the further down into the dark valley you can see as well. And there's always, on the journey towards truth, like an offer of the detour into nihilism.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If there's only one of you and you have a vote and it's thumbs up or thumbs down, how can you be conflicted?", "author": "Jack Kelley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/d548e142-2d5c-455e-8a3c-bc08780bea32/JACK-KELLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
